  September 8, 2025

ROLL CALL: At 6:06 p.m., on Monday, September 8, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez, Public Information Specialist
Rodriguez

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Lee

LEE: Mayor Lee read the City’s Mission Statement as follows: The City of Alhambra is dedicated to
responsive, creative leadership and quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a
supportive business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIAL

1.  COMMENDATIONS: AYSO REGION 60 16U BOYS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TEAM ––
  F2M25-3

  Mayor Lee and the Alhambra City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to
  congratulate and commend the American Youth Soccer Region 60 16 and under Boys Division
  Team for their victory in the 16 and under Boys Division National Championship Tournament.
  The National Championship games spanned six days, featured 1,031 games played across
  25 soccer fields, and brought together over 4,800 players, 696 coaches, 348 teams, and filled
  over 3,000 referee slots. The win marked the first time the Region won the National Title. The
  AYSO Region 60 players were to be commended for demonstrating their athletic skills, their
  ability to work together in a spirit of commitment, dedication and hard work and for becoming
  National Champions. Mayor Lee presented commendations to the AYSO Region 16U Boys
  National Championship Team members and coaches as follows:

3.  CONSIDERATION OF AN ORDINANCE TO DESIGNATE FIRE HAZARD SEVERITY
  ZONES (FHSZ) WITHIN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 51178 AND THE CALIFORNIA FIRE CODE – F2M25-49,
  O2M25-4849

  Fire Chief RAGUSA delivered the staff report and presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. Pursuant to State law, the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
  (CAL FIRE) - Office of the State Fire Marshal periodically updates Fire Hazard Severity Zone
  (FHSZ) maps for Local Responsibility Areas throughout the State. These maps identify varying
  levels of fire hazard (Moderate, High, and Very High) based on factors including vegetation,
  topography, weather, crown fire potential, fire history, and ember production and movement.
  State law requires local jurisdictions to designate FHSZ within their boundaries by ordinance
  to ensure proper implementation of associated building standards and fire safety requirements
  within identified zones. On March 24, 2025, CAL FIRE completed its latest assessment and
  released a map identifying FHSZ within the City of Alhambra. The City of Alhambra has not
  been included in the CAL FIRE FHSZ maps in the past. In the newly released maps,
  approximately less than one acre in Alhambra has been classified under the Very High
  Severity Zone designation. There are two parcels affected on Sherwood Avenue and two
  parcels on Keats Street. The City posted the map and information regarding FHSZ on the
  City’s website at https://www.alhambraca.gov/863/FireHazard-Severity-Zones.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St. discussed the wildfires in
  Altadena and Pacific Palisades, changes to the Fire Hazard Severity Zones, and how to
  implement the maps.

  Discussion: Councilmember WANG and Chief RAGUSA discussed the impact on
  Alhambra residents in the limited parcels with regards to vegetation management and fire
  inspections. They also discussed how to notify impacted residents. Mayor LEE and Chief
  RAGUSA discussed the changes to the maps which now included Alhambra.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M25-4849: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City
  Council to designate Fire Hazard Severity Zones

  which ordinance would return at a subsequent meeting for a second reading and consideration
  for adoption.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded: ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  REPORT REGARDING AGENDA PLACEMENT OF PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-
  AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M24-7

  City Clerk MYLES delivered a staff report. At the January 13, 2025 Council meeting, at
  3
9-8-25
   Council’s direction, staff presented the results of a survey regarding where public comment for
  non-agendized items was placed on the agendas of surrounding cities. After receiving public
  comment and City Council discussion, the Council directed the agenda item of public comment
  for non-agendized items be temporarily set to the beginning of the meeting, after any
  Ceremonial items, for an initial set time of 30 minutes for a 6-month period and directed staff
  return with a report after that timeframe. In summary, there have been nine regular City Council
  meetings since the placement of public comment for non-agendized items was temporarily
  moved to the beginning of the meeting. Out of those nine meetings, the majority of individuals
  wishing to speak on a non-agendized item were able to do so during the initial 30-minute
  period. The average number of speakers during the initial public comment period was six. In
  those six instances where there were speakers during the continuation of public comment for
  non-agendized items at the end of the meeting, the average number of speakers was two. If it
  was the desire of the City Council to make this a permanent change, upon direction from the
  Council, staff could prepare an ordinance amending Chapter 2.04.030 of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code pertaining to the order of business for Council meetings for Council’s
  consideration at the next regular meeting.

  Public Comment:
  1) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., supported the 30 minutes allotted for Public Comment at
  the beginning of City Council meetings.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., supported Public Comment at the beginning of City
  Council meetings.

  Discussion:  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER supported continuing Public
  comment for Non-Agendized items at the beginning of the meeting, but suggested staff
  research what other agencies allowed for public comment in order to accommodate as many
  public speakers as possible. Vice Mayor MALONEY spoke in support of the current practice
  to allow for speakers at the beginning of the meeting. He also supported reducing the individual
  speaking time to accommodate a large volume of speakers. He referred staff to review the
  City of San Luis Obispo’s practices which allows for 3 minutes individual speaking time at the
  beginning of the meeting and 5 minutes at the end of the meeting. Councilmember MAZA
  supported the current practice of public comment at the beginning of the meeting and
  supported Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s suggestion to review other agencies practices. He also
  supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion to reduce speaking time at the beginning of the meeting
  compared to the end. He further suggested staff consider condensing speaking time when
  individuals have multiple items they wish to speak on which would allow for others time to
  speak. Councilmember WANG echoed Mr. Maza’s comments and supported Public Comment
  for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning of the meeting. She also supported suggestions
  made by her fellow Councilmembers and further discussed other means for the public to
  contact Councilmembers through phone or email. Mayor LEE spoke in support of Public
  Comment for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning of the meeting and discussed the initial
  staff report and information regarding other agencies’ practices with respect to public
  comment. She supported Mr. Maloney’s suggestion of reducing the time to 3 minutes during
  the initial 30-minute timeframe for Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items and then 5
  minutes during the continuation of the item at the end of the meeting. She supported Mr.
  Maza’s suggestion but stated that she would like more information regarding the consent
  agenda.

  Ms. LEE and City Attorney MONTES discussed Council’s direction to staff. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the research staff conducted regarding
  other agencies 9 months ago and the types of research they could further conduct based on
  Council’s comments. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to direct staff to research the
  practices of other cities and agencies based on Council’s comments and directed them to
  return with a report at the next City Council meeting. Mr. MAZA seconded the motion and
  added that Council was aware that they could be flexible in trying new practices and continue
  4
9-8-25
   to refine them as needed.

  Action Taken:  Council directed staff to return with more information on whether
  surrounding cities have set time limits for public comment on non-agendized items and for
  consent agenda items.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, WANG, MALONEY, MAZA, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL SCADA SERVICES AND MAINTENANCE FOR
  THE WATER AND SEWER DIVISIONS – F2M25-45, RFP2M25-13, C2M25-39, M2M25-131

  On July 28, 2025 the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals (RFP)
  for SCADA Professional Services and Maintenance for the Water and Sewer Divisions. There
  were eight proposals received for the project. Staff conducted a review and evaluation of the
  responding proposals and found the Strategic Engineering & Automation Systems proposal
  the best suited for the City’s SCADA needs.

  Discussion:  None.

  Divisions, in an amount not to exceed $140,000.00 for one year, with two additional two-year

  Amendment No. 3 was to clarify language in the existing agreement. Since the issuance of

14.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION ORDINANCE APPROVING ZONING TEXT
  AMENDMENT AMD-25-03, AMENDING TITLE 23 (ZONING) OF THE ALHAMBRA
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCORPORATE CHAPTER 23.23 (HISTORIC PRESERVATION)
  AND OTHER ASSOCIATED AMENDMENTS, AND AMENDING CHAPTER 2.41 (HISTORIC
  PRESERVATION COMMISSION) – F2M20-51, O2M25-4848

  Staff requested that the City Council declare introduced for second reading and adopt a
  Historic Preservation Ordinance (O2M25-4848). Ordinance No. O2M25-4848 approving
  Zoning Text Amendment AMD-25-03 is a City-initiated application to adopt a Historic
  Preservation Ordinance establishing regulations and standards for designating historic
  resources within the City and regulating designated resources as part of a comprehensive
  Historic Preservation Program, as well as amending various sections of the Alhambra
  Municipal Code to establish consistency with the proposed Historic Preservation Ordinance.
  Adoption and implementation of a Historic Preservation Ordinance would align with the goals,
  policies, and objectives set forth in the City’s General Plan and the City Council 2025 Strategic
  Plan. The revised Historic Preservation Ordinance would establish regulations and standards
  for the treatment of historic resources City-wide that were intended to: 1.) Balance the interests
  of the community and individual property owners; 2.) Provide recognition of and protection for
  existing historic resources; 3.) Establish incentives to encourage rehabilitation and
  preservation of historic resources; and 4.) Add predictability to the local development process.
  The Ordinance, which would apply City-wide, establishes the process for determining a
  property’s status as a historic resource. Statuses included: (1) eligible or potentially eligible
  individual resource; (2) contributor or non-contributor in an eligible or potentially eligible historic
  district; (3) designated landmark; or (4) contributor or non-contributor in a designated historic
  district. The City Council gave first reading to this ordinance at the August 25, 2025 Council
  meeting.

  Public Comment:  Brian OTIS, 320 N. Monterey St., spoke in support of the Ordinance
  as a life long resident and spoke regarding the importance of historic preservation.

  Discussion:  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff and the community for
  their work.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopted
  the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M25-4848: AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA ADOPTING ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT AMD-
  25-03, AMENDING TITLE 23 (ZONING) OF THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL

  2.41 (HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION)

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS CONTINUED – F2M25-4

2) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, spoke in support of Item No. 14. She went on to discuss her concerns
